key_insight: Algebraic World Model (AWM) turns interaction with unfamiliar environments into executable mathematical models and Lean 4 proofs of reachability or impossibility.
engineering_relevance: AWM connects exploratory agents with formal verification, producing inspectable rules and machine-checked guarantees relative to a learned environment model.
method: Explore the environment, then test and revise executable Python hypotheses against observations.
Organize hypotheses into typed objects and shared rules, simplifying them through category-theory-guided transformations.
Formalize the resulting model in Lean 4 to certify winning trajectories or prove goals unreachable.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports kernel-checked impossibility proofs in all six runs across two impossible levels, versus none in 12 baseline runs, and Lean replay of winning trajectories for all 183 levels across 25 public ARC-AGI-3 games.
watch_item: Lean verifies claims about the formalized model; applying those guarantees to the environment depends on the learned rules faithfully capturing its mechanics.
paper_title: Algebraic World Model: From Exploration to Proofs
